question:
I am trying to understand the introduction of package-lock.yml in the DBT Documentation for Upgrading to 1.7

However, it is not quite clear how --upgrade option works.

It seems to work the same without or without --upgrade.

If there is no change in the package.yml, package-lock.yml remains the same (w/ or w/o --upgrade)

And if the package.yml gets a new version, in both the case, the package-lock.yml gets updates with the revisions. (w/ or w/o --upgrade)

The sentence:

To retain the behavior prior to v1.7, there are two main options:
1. Use dbt deps --upgrade everywhere dbt deps was used previously.
:

Might require clarification.
title: Use of `--upgrade` option in DBT 1.7 - `dbt deps` for package-lock.yml
answer:
dbt deps will just install what's defined in your package-lock.yml, while dbt deps --upgrade will also look for potential upgrades given your version parameters in packages.yml.

But this is simpler using an example.

Say this is your packages.yml below:

packages:
  - package: calogica/dbt_expectations
    version: [">=0.10.0", "<0.11.0"]

then, you run dbt deps on your project for the first time, and this is your package-lock.yml that gets created:

packages:
  - package: calogica/dbt_expectations
    version: 0.10.4

From now on, every time you run dbt deps in your project (e.g. after a dbt clean), it will just install whatever version is defined in the package-lock.yml file.

On the other hand, imagine that a new patch version is up for your package (e.g. calogica/dbt_expectations went up from v0.10.4 to v0.10.5). In order for you to upgrade to that newer version, you will need to run a dbt deps --upgrade.
